newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: CRICKET-BRANDES AND STREAK MAKE INDIA STRUGGLE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BRANDES AND STREAK MAKE INDIA STRUGGLE.

text.p: Zimbabwe pacemen Eddo Brandes and Heath Streak exploited helpful conditions to share seven wickets as India were bowled out for 168 in the first one-day international on Saturday.

Only opener Vikram Rathore (34), former test captain Mohammad Azharuddin (24) and all-rounder Robin Singh (45) made scores of any substance in a match reduced from 50 to 44 overs after light drizzle delayed the start by 45 minutes.

Brandes, Zimbabwe's leading wicket-taker with a haul of 55 in one-day internationals, struck critical blows by removing captain Sachin tendulkar and Mohammad Azharuddin on a pitch offering both bounce and movement off the seam.
Brandes finished with two for 34 while strike bowler Streak took two middle order wickets and then came back strongly to mop up the tail for a career-best five for 32.
There were only two productive partnerships after India were put in to bat, Rathore and Azharuddin sharing a third-wicket stand of 35 and Singh and Anil Kumble (20) adding 64 for the seventh wicket.

Reduced to a meagre 95 for six in the 30th over, India were then boosted by some intelligent batting from the left-handed Singh. In tandem with Kumble, he took his team beyond the 150-mark, striking three fours in his 63-ball 45.

Tendulkar threatened a repeat of his explosive 45 against South Africa in the triangular series final in Durban on Thursday night when he imperiously drove fast bowler Brandes for six over wide long-off in the third over of the innings.
But, two overs later, he was undone by a bouncing delivery from Brandes as he attempted to drive. He edged the ball to Grant Flower at second slip to depart for 13.
